body.p: Shaejjámi [caiman] was Ese'ejja [human] and lived on the bank of the river. There was a toad, tapacáca, that had fire. One day this man, tapacáca, met with shaejjámi, he set fire to him and the caiman began to burn. He burned strongly for a long time, and this person, shaejjámi, came out in the form of a caiman. Angrily, he killed tapacáca and said, "I am caiman now, when any Ese'ejja bathes in the river, I will eat him, he will serve as my food." This is why the caiman now bites and eats the people who bathe where he is.
